title: Elon Musk: every hand he played (Dagar Unfiltered)

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon Musk has gone all in more times than any sane person should.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And somehow, the house still hasn't figured out how to stop him.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Every big moment in his life is basically the same move. Put everything on the table. Hope the cards are good.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So let's look at every hand he's played.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Hand number one. Pretoria, South Africa, 1971.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon is the kid who reads everything. When he runs out of books, he reads the encyclopedia. For fun.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At school he's small, nerdy, and badly bullied. So he hides in computers.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At twelve, he writes a space shooter game called Blastar, and sells it to a magazine for five hundred dollars.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Twelve years old, and already selling space stuff. Some things never change.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: At seventeen, he leaves for Canada with almost nothing. Then the US. Physics, economics.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 1995, he starts a PhD at Stanford. He lasts two days.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two days. Some people take longer to return a pair of shoes.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Because the internet is exploding, and Elon wants in.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: With his brother Kimbal, he starts Zip2, online city guides for newspapers.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Money is so tight, he sleeps in the office and showers at the YMCA.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then in 1999, Compaq buys Zip2 for 307 million dollars. Elon's cut is 22 million. He's twenty seven.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So naturally, he buys a million dollar McLaren F1. A few months later, he crashes it. No insurance.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: First hand, won. Barely kept the car.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Hand number two. He goes all in again, on an online bank called X.com.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It merges with a rival and becomes a little thing called PayPal.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2000, while he's on a plane, the board fires him as CEO.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Fired from your own company while you're in the air. That's cold.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But in 2002, eBay buys PayPal for 1.5 billion dollars, and Elon walks away with around 180 million.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Any normal person retires to a beach here.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon looks at that money and thinks, rockets.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Hand number three. The big one.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He wants humans on Mars. So he flies to Russia to buy old missiles.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It goes badly. Turns out, can I get a discount on your missiles, is not a great opening line.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: On the flight home, he decides to build his own. SpaceX. 2002.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then he puts millions into a tiny electric car startup called Tesla.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two of the hardest businesses on the planet. At the same time.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Falcon 1, flight one. 2006. It crashes.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Flight two. 2007. It fails.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Flight three. August 2008. It fails again.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Tesla's Roadster costs way more to build than anyone planned. Then the financial crisis hits.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: His marriage ends. He's borrowing money from friends to pay rent.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He later called 2008 the worst year of his life.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And here's the move. He takes almost everything he has left, and splits it between both companies.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Enough for one more launch.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: September 28th, 2008. Falcon 1, flight four.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And holy shit. It reaches orbit.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Days before Christmas, NASA hands SpaceX a 1.6 billion dollar contract.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: And on Christmas Eve, at the last possible moment, Tesla's funding comes through.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Two companies, saved in the same week. Santa was clearly a fan.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Hand number four. Now he's got chips, and he plays fast.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: 2012. SpaceX's Dragon becomes the first commercial spacecraft to visit the space station.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Tesla's Model S shows up, and suddenly electric cars are cool.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: 2015. A Falcon 9 booster flies to space, comes back, and lands standing up. A rocket that parks itself.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: 2018. Falcon Heavy launches with his own cherry red Tesla on top, and a dummy in a spacesuit behind the wheel.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It's still out there, looping around the Sun. The most expensive way ever to avoid traffic.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But not every bet is a rocket. Some are tweets.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2018, he tweets that he might take Tesla private. Funding secured.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: It wasn't. Regulators fined him and Tesla 20 million dollars each.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then the Cybertruck reveal. Unbreakable glass. His designer throws a metal ball at it. It breaks. On stage. Twice.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Hand number five. The most expensive impulse buy in history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In 2022, he offers 44 billion dollars for Twitter. Then tries to back out. Then buys it anyway.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He walks into headquarters carrying a sink. Let that sink in.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: He fires most of the staff, sells the blue checks, and renames the whole thing X.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then in 2025, he goes to Washington to run a cost cutting team called DOGE. Hero to some. Villain to others. A few months later, he's out.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Meanwhile in Texas, SpaceX is building the biggest rocket ever made. Starship.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The first one, in 2023, blows up. SpaceX calls it a rapid unscheduled disassembly.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Which is engineer for, it blew the fuck up.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But in October 2024, the booster flies back to the tower, and the tower catches it with two giant metal arms.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Hand number six. 2026.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: In June, SpaceX goes public. It raises 75 billion dollars. The biggest stock market debut ever.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: By the end of day one, Forbes says Elon is worth about 1.1 trillion dollars. The first trillionaire in history.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The guy with three crashed rockets and borrowed rent money.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So, genius or lucky?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Honestly, maybe the real answer is simpler.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Most people who go all in, lose everything. And you never hear about them.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Elon went all in six times. And he's still sitting at the table.
